name: George Francis Adams (#2)
notable_stories: Known locally in Douglas County, Oregon, as the owner of the Adams Drug Store
Died from influenza-pneumonia at the tail end of the 1918-1920 pandemic
Victim of the 1918–1920 flu epidemic (per John Howard's memoir)
1930 census listed his son George F. Adams Sr. as George F. Wells, step-son because Arthur Wells was step-father
He died of influenza at the tail end of the flu pandemic, which lingered for about three years and reached isolated areas such as rural Oregon.
milestones: Married Serena Marie Nevada Trumbo (m. 7 Jan 1909, Lewis County, WA)
Graduated from Washington State University with a degree in Pharmacy (1908)
Military: Enlisted 2 June 1898, Denver, CO (Spanish–American War era)
Married Serena Marie Nevada Nini Trumbo (7 January 1909, Lewis County, WA)
Census trail: Denver CO (1880, 1900) → Umpqua, Douglas County OR (1910) → Sutherlin OR (1920)
Served in the military on 2 Jun 1898 in Denver, CO
Military: Military service entry dated 2 Jun 1898, Denver, Arapahoe County, CO.
Military: George F. Adams served in the military in Denver in 1898; the branch is not stated.
Census 1920: Douglas County, Oregon, head of household, aged 43, born Missouri, with Serena (30), Presley N. (9), Edith V. (7) and Edward G. (3 years 9 months)
Buried at Valley View Cemetery, Sutherlin, Oregon
education: Graduated from Washington State University with a degree in Pharmacy in 1908
Pharmacy degree from Washington State University, Pullman, WA, 1908.
career: Owner of the Adams Drug Store in Sutherlin, Oregon; described as one of the best known citizens of Douglas County (Journal of the National Association of Retail Druggists, 26 Feb 1920)
He worked in a pharmacy, where an article says George Trumbo worked with him.

On his children's birth certificates he is a druggist or pharmacist, born in Missouri: at Roseburg in 1910 (aged 33) and 1916, and at Sutherlin in 1912 (aged 35).

Born 24 Aug 1876 in Chariton County, Missouri; registered for the WWI draft in 1917 at Sutherlin as a druggist in his own business; died 7 Feb 1920 at Oakland, Douglas County, and buried at Valley View Cemetery, Sutherlin (Turner / Harvey Family Tree, citing Find a Grave memorial 83796381, with photographs of his headstone, "George F. Adams 1876–1920").
